subject.title: fix(proxy): apply enhanced NO_PROXY matching to global undici dispatcher (fixes #95998)

question: Should OpenClaw accept `proxy.enhancedNoProxy` as an opt-in process-wide direct-bypass mode, and should that mode apply only to inherited env proxy routing or also to managed `proxy.enabled=true` routing?
rationale: The code direction can be repaired mechanically, but this setting changes operator egress expectations and the current docs imply behavior across a managed-proxy boundary that the implementation does not provide.

options.title: Clarify env-proxy-only scope first
options.body: Keep the default-off setting, document it as inherited EnvHttpProxyAgent routing for CIDR/octet-wildcard support, and make managed-proxy behavior explicitly out of scope unless separately designed.

options.title: Extend managed proxy behavior too
options.body: Require an explicit managed-proxy bypass design, tests, and docs before merge so `proxy.enabled=true` users get the behavior the network-proxy page implies.

options.title: Reject the core config surface
options.body: Close or supersede this branch if maintainers prefer a narrower bug fix without adding a process-wide proxy-bypass knob.

recommendation.title: Clarify env-proxy-only scope first
recommendation.body: Keep the default-off setting, document it as inherited EnvHttpProxyAgent routing for CIDR/octet-wildcard support, and make managed-proxy behavior explicitly out of scope unless separately designed.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent no-proxy global dispatcher history and were specifically asked to review this network-boundary change in the PR discussion.
